analysis.title: Rising yields raise the portfolio appeal of bonds and diversified investing (UBS House View - Daily Asia)
key_insights: Global bond yields rose on recalibrated rate expectations and a rebound in equity appetite, hurting fixed income holders. The German 2-year yield ended 12bps higher last week, its sharpest weekly rise in two months.

Japanese 10-year yields reached their highest level since 22 October, moving with higher US yields on news that President Trump was not seeking a peace deal with Iran and on Fed President Waller's comments about a possible 50bps rate hike at the Fed's December meeting.

UBS argues that elevated starting yields have restored the appeal of the traditional 60/40 portfolio. High-quality bonds now offer meaningful income, potential capital appreciation if growth slows, and a cushion against some equity declines.

Higher starting yields increase bond income and provide a larger buffer against losses if rates rise further. They also create room for price gains if inflation moderates, growth weakens or central banks eventually cut rates.

The 60/40 portfolio is not guaranteed to offset every equity decline. High-quality bonds have historically diversified equities better when inflation is low or stable. If inflation stays elevated and rates rise, stocks and bonds can fall together.

UBS recommends completion assets alongside the core: hedge funds for returns when stocks and bonds both come under pressure, commodities for low correlation and supply-constraint or inflation protection, and private infrastructure for inflation-linked income. It flags private investments' illiquidity, limited disclosure, uncertain cash flows, leverage, capital calls and blind-pool risk.

UBS rates high grade and investment grade bonds Attractive, favoring short- to medium-duration high-quality bonds and staying cautious on the longest maturities because of fiscal concerns and elevated issuance. It also rates high yield and emerging market bonds Attractive on elevated yields and resilient aggregate fundamentals.
A 60/40 US equity-bond portfolio left untouched since 2020 would have drifted to about 80/20. UBS recommends regular rebalancing to restore the intended risk profile.
